standard.title: Design movement strategies
standard.description: design and demonstrate how movement strategies can be manipulated to improve movement outcomes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have transferred familiar movement strategies to different movement situations and can identify when strategies are or are not working (Y5-6). They can describe how strategies affect movement outcomes in broad terms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design and demonstrate how movement strategies can be manipulated to improve movement outcomes across a range of movement situations.

nodes.label: Understanding movement strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and name movement strategies relevant to at least one movement context and describe what each strategy is intended to achieve.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two movement strategies applicable to one movement scenario and explain what each is trying to achieve.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe movement strategies across game categories and movement forms; explain the intended outcome of each strategy in terms of space, possession, scoring or performance quality.
wider: Compare movement strategies across different game categories (invasion, net/court, target) and identify shared principles that apply across all three
Investigate how static and dynamic balance underpin movement strategies in both game-based and performance contexts, identifying the common biomechanical basis
nodes.hinge_reason: Design requires a repertoire of strategies to draw from — students who cannot name and explain existing strategies cannot make purposeful design decisions. Without this conceptual base, design becomes guessing rather than deliberate manipulation.

response_modes.reason: Build a working vocabulary of movement strategies through exposure across contexts. Students need multiple strategy types on which to draw before they can make design choices.

success_criteria: Names at least two movement strategies for a given context
Explains the intended movement outcome of each strategy

nodes.label: Selecting and adapting strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select a movement strategy appropriate to a specific scenario, justifying the selection, and adapt previously successful strategies to new movement challenges.
nodes.minimum_width: Select one movement strategy for a given scenario and give at least one reason why it is appropriate for that context.
nodes.typical_width: Select and apply strategies across several movement scenarios; draw on previously successful strategies and adapt them to new challenges; explain adaptations made and predicted outcomes.
wider: Predict the effectiveness of changes in tactics or strategies on scoring opportunities in a game and suggest reasons for unexpected results — applying this cycle across multiple game forms
Explore similarities between bases of support and flow of movements across different movement sequences requiring static and dynamic balance, selecting strategies that exploit these shared principles

response_modes.reason: Strategy selection becomes meaningful only when students encounter varied scenarios that require different selections. Multiple contexts prevent strategy fixation on one default approach.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The breadth of movement contexts in which students practise strategy selection determines the transferability of their strategic thinking. Rich width here develops genuine game sense rather than context-specific habits.
success_criteria: Selects a movement strategy appropriate to a specific scenario
Gives at least one reason why the strategy suits the context or challenge

nodes.label: Designing and demonstrating movement strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design a movement strategy for a specific scenario, implement it, and evaluate whether the design achieved the intended improvement in the movement outcome.
nodes.minimum_width: Design one movement strategy for a specific scenario, implement it, and comment on whether it produced the intended improvement.
nodes.typical_width: Design and implement movement strategies across a range of scenarios; predict outcomes before implementation; evaluate actual outcomes against predictions; explain how design choices related to space, balance, flow or tactics influenced the result.
wider: Design movement strategies for non-traditional or student-invented game scenarios, evaluating how strategic principles generalise to unfamiliar contexts

Develop and implement a strategy for a complex movement challenge involving multiple variables (e.g. changing teams, modified rules) and document how the strategy was adjusted in response to unexpected outcomes

response_modes.reason: Design integrates strategy knowledge, selection judgement and implementation — instruction should scaffold the full design-implement-evaluate cycle, not just the planning phase.

success_criteria: Designs a movement strategy for a specified scenario with at least one explicit design rationale
Evaluates whether the strategy achieved the intended movement outcome improvement
